spec_match.rationale: Targets the feature's defining cascade contract — the * argument contributes zero specificity — with a measured experiment, plus a shipped-surface control proving the measurement method.

interactive.rationale: Order-flipping button groups rebuild a real constructed stylesheet rule by rule and the painted colour is read back via getComputedStyle(el, '::highlight(name)').

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the order-flip experiment with computed-style readback; the page runs exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers per-rule insertRule rejection reporting, the no-registry branch, the equal-specificity control in both orders, and an explicit spec-violation message should a build ever let the universal rule win.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5174965228929024 and the css-pseudo-4 highlight-styling section.

conformance.rationale: The suite's universal-zero-specificity assertion runs this page's Experiment B as an automated check with named-rule-first ordering.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud fallback, no chrome-devtools-mcp): Experiment A measured both orders — yellow-last read back rgb(254,240,138), blue-last rgb(219,234,254), last rule winning as required; Experiment B honestly reported the universal rule's SyntaxError with the named BLUE still painting; zero console errors; both viewports screenshotted.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts registration, the order-wins control result, the zero-specificity verdict when runnable, and the labelled fallback when the parser rejects the rule.

design_system.rationale: Token colours only (fef08a/dbeafe resolved at runtime for comparison), AAA verdict colours, 44px buttons with outline pressed state.

accessibility.rationale: Button groups are labelled, results land in role=status aria-live readouts as text (colour names, not just swatches), and the experiment is fully keyboard-operable.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×800: zero overflow, identical measured results on both.

openQuestions.title: Run Experiment B decisively on a 158+/flagged engine
openQuestions.detail: With CSSCustomHighlightUniversalSelector active, the named-first/universal-LAST order must still read back BLUE — capture that measurement (and the universal-first order) to turn this page's honest fallback into recorded positive evidence, and confirm the conformance suite's universal-zero-specificity assertion passes.

guidanceConsulted.query: highlight text ranges in page without extra DOM spans
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Set ranges on text nodes and register one Highlight per styling concern.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The cascade-demo highlight is a single Range on the paragraph's text node; the experiment varies only the stylesheet, isolating the cascade variable.

guidanceConsulted.query: feature detect CSS value support graceful fallback
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Probe the exact surface and keep detection falsifiable rather than inferring from adjacent support.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Rules are inserted individually via insertRule so the unsupported universal rule fails alone and is reported with its error name; support is never inferred from the named form working.

summary: The zero-specificity contract as a falsifiable experiment: a working equal-specificity control measured in both orders on Chromium 141 (yellow/blue readbacks flip with source order), and the universal-vs-named test honestly reporting the pre-158 SyntaxError until a flagged engine can run it decisively. Cloud headless verification, both viewports clean.
